note: THE SECOND MISSING PIECE, which the frontier probe could not see because it stops at the first raise. Emacs answers ("cba" "ab"); kg answers (wrong-type-argument stringp (99 98 97)). Once `multibyte-string-p' exists and answers nil, `s-reverse' runs its else branch and lands on `(concat LIST-OF-CHARACTERS)' -- kg's `concat' takes strings only, so binding the predicate alone leaves s-reverse raising, one name further along. So the demand behind `multibyte-string-p' is TWO names deep and F.1 has to bind both; `string-to-list' and `nreverse' are already kg's and already agree. It also fixes what the reversal MEANS in kg: `string-to-list' decodes UTF-8 into codepoints, so the concat arm reassembles characters and kg's `s-reverse' reverses BY CHARACTER, not by byte, which corrects what this phase's plan predicted.
